items.t: Mild to moderate hypertension (in severe hypertension only where standard therapy is ineffective or inappropriate); congestive heart failure (with diuretics and, when appropriate, digitalis and beta-blockers); myocardial infarction (short-term treatment within 24 hours, and long-term prevention of symptomatic heart failure in stable patients with left ventricular dysfunction, ejection fraction < 40%); macroproteinuric diabetic nephropathy in insulin-dependent (type 1) diabetes.

src.q: Hypertension: The management of mild to moderate hypertension. In severe hypertension it should be used where standard therapy is ineffective or inappropriate.
Captopril is indicated for the treatment of congestive heart failure.
Captopril is indicated in any clinically stable patient within the first 24 hours of an infarction.
Captopril is indicated in insulin dependent diabetics for the treatment of macroproteinuric diabetic nephropathy
The drug should be used together with diuretics and, when appropriate, digitalis and beta-blockers.
Captopril is indicated in clinically stable patients with asymptomatic and symptomatic left ventricular dysfunction (ejection fraction < 40%)

items.t: Heart failure: use under specialist supervision if the dose is over 100 mg daily (with or without a diuretic), in severe renal impairment, or in severe congestive heart failure.

src.q: In patients on doses of over 100 mg daily plus or minus a diuretic, in those with severe renal impairment or those with severe congestive heart failure use of captopril should be under specialist supervision.

items.t: Dual RAAS blockade (ACE inhibitor with an angiotensin II receptor blocker or aliskiren) only if absolutely necessary, under specialist supervision with frequent close monitoring.

src.q: If dual blockade therapy is considered absolutely necessary, this should only occur under specialist supervision and subject to frequent close monitoring of renal function, electrolytes and blood pressure.

items.t: Start 25-50 mg daily in two divided doses; increase at intervals of at least 2 weeks to 100-150 mg/day in two divided doses as needed. Recommended maximum 150 mg daily. Once daily may suit when a thiazide diuretic is added.

src.q: The recommended starting dose is 25-50mg daily in two divided doses.
The dose may be increased incrementally, with intervals of at least 2 weeks, to 100-150 mg/day in two divided doses as needed to reach target blood pressure.
The recommended maximum daily dose is 150mg.
A once-daily dosing regimen may be appropriate when concomitant antihypertensive medication such as thiazide diuretics is added.

items.t: Strongly active renin-angiotensin system (hypovolaemia, renovascular hypertension, cardiac decompensation): start with a single 6.25 mg or 12.5 mg dose, preferably under close medical supervision; then give these doses twice a day, increasing gradually to 50 mg per day and, if needed, 100 mg per day (in one or two doses).

src.q: it is preferable to commence with a single dose of 6.25 mg or 12.5 mg.
The inauguration of this treatment should preferably take place under close medical supervision.
These doses will then be administered at a rate of two per day.
The dosage can be gradually increased to 50mg per day in one or two doses and if necessary to 100mg per day in one or two doses.

items.t: Start under close medical supervision at 6.25-12.5 mg two or three times daily; titrate at intervals of at least 2 weeks to a maintenance dose of 75-150 mg per day, maximum 150 mg per day in divided doses.

src.q: Treatment with captopril for congestive heart failure should be initiated under close medical supervision.
The usual starting dose is 6.25mg - 12.5mg BID or TID.
up to a maximum of 150mg per day in divided doses.
Titration to the maintenance dose (75-150mg per day)
The dose should be increased incrementally, with intervals of at least 2 weeks to evaluate patient's response.

items.t: Short-term (start in hospital, stable haemodynamics): 6.25 mg test dose, 12.5 mg 2 hours later, 25 mg 12 hours later; then 100 mg/day in two doses for 4 weeks. Chronic (start day 3-16, in hospital): 6.25 mg, then 12.5 mg three times daily for 2 days, then 25 mg three times daily; long-term 75-150 mg daily in two or three doses.

src.q: A 6.25mg test dose should be administered, with a 12.5mg dose being administered 2 hours afterwards and a 25mg dose 12 hours later.
captopril should be administered in a 100mg/day dose, in two daily administrations, for 4 weeks
Treatment should be initiated with a dose of 6.25mg followed by 12.5mg 3 times daily for 2 days and then 25mg 3 times daily
The recommended dose for effective cardioprotection during long-term treatment is 75 to 150mg daily in two or three doses.
Captopril treatment should begin in hospital as soon as possible following the appearance of the signs and/or symptoms in patients with stable haemodynamics.
it is suggested that treatment be instigated between the 3rd and 16th day post-infarction
Treatment should be started in hospital under strict surveillance (particularly of blood pressure) until the 75mg dose is reached.

items.t: 75-100 mg daily in divided doses.

src.q: the recommended daily dose is 75-100mg in divided doses.

items.t: Elderly: consider a lower starting dose (6.25 mg twice daily); titrate to blood pressure and keep the dose as low as possible.

src.q: consideration should be given to initiating therapy with a lower starting dose (6.25 mg BID) in elderly patients
Dosage should be titrated against the blood pressure response and kept as low as possible to achieve adequate control.

items.t: Efficacy and safety not fully established. Start under close medical supervision. Initial dose about 0.3 mg/kg; 0.15 mg/kg in children with renal dysfunction, premature infants, newborns and infants. Usually given 3 times a day, adjusted to response.

src.q: The efficacy and safety of captopril have not been fully established. The use of captopril in children and adolescents should be initiated under close medical supervision.
The initial dose of captopril is about 0.3mg/kg body weight.
the starting dose should be only 0.15 mg captopril/kg weight.
Generally, captopril is administered to children 3 times a day

items.t: Infants, especially newborns, may be more susceptible to haemodynamic effects: excessive, prolonged and unpredictable falls in blood pressure with oliguria and seizures have been reported.

src.q: Infants, especially new-borns, may be more susceptible to the adverse haemodynamic effects of captopril.
Excessive, prolonged and unpredictable decreases in blood pressure and associated complications, including oliguria and seizures have been reported.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to captopril, any other ACE inhibitor or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

src.q: Lactation (see section 4.6)

items.t: With sacubitril/valsartan; do not start captopril within 36 hours of the last sacubitril/valsartan dose.

src.q: Concomitant use with sacubitril/valsartan therapy. Captopril must not be initiated earlier than 36 hours after the last dose of sacubitril/valsartan

items.t: Symptomatic hypotension: more likely with volume or sodium depletion (vigorous diuretics, salt restriction, diarrhoea, vomiting, haemodialysis) and in heart failure. Correct depletion first and consider a lower starting dose. Excessive falls in ischaemic heart or cerebrovascular disease may cause MI or stroke.

src.q: Volume and/or sodium depletion should be corrected before the administration of an ACE inhibitor and a lower starting dose should be considered.
Patients with heart failure are at higher risk of hypotension and a lower starting dose is recommended when initiating therapy with an ACE inhibitor.
excessive blood pressure lowering in patients with ischaemic cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease may increase the risk of myocardial infarction or stroke.

items.t: Bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis to a single kidney: higher risk of hypotension and renal insufficiency; start under close supervision with low doses, careful titration and renal monitoring.

src.q: In these patients, therapy should be initiated under close medical supervision with low doses, careful titration and monitoring of renal function.

items.t: Renal impairment (CrCl 40 mL/min or less): adjust starting dose to creatinine clearance; monitor potassium and creatinine. The SmPC also states that patients with renal impairment should not normally be treated with captopril.

src.q: In cases of renal impairment (creatinine clearance ≤40ml/min), the initial dosage of captopril must be adjusted according to the patient's creatinine clearance
Patients with renal impairment should not normally be treated with captopril.

items.t: Angioedema can occur at any time, including after months or years; stop promptly. Tongue, glottis or larynx involvement may be fatal and needs emergency treatment. Higher incidence in black patients. Intestinal angioedema can present as abdominal pain.

src.q: Angioedema involving the tongue, glottis or larynx may be fatal.
Black patients receiving ACE inhibitors have been reported to have a higher incidence of angioedema compared to non-blacks.
Intestinal angioedema should be included in the differential diagnosis of patients on ACE inhibitors presenting with abdominal pain

items.t: Neutropenia/agranulocytosis: use with extreme caution with pre-existing renal impairment, collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, allopurinol or procainamide. Check white cell and differential counts before treatment, every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then periodically. Stop if neutrophils below 1000/mm3.

src.q: Captopril should be used with extreme caution in patients with pre-existing impaired renal function, collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, treatment with allopurinol or procainamide
every 2 weeks during the first 3 months of captopril therapy, and periodically thereafter.
should be withdrawn if neutropenia (neutrophils less than 1000/mm3) is detected or suspected.

items.t: Hyperkalaemia risk with renal insufficiency, diabetes, hypoaldosteronism, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, heparin, trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole, aldosterone antagonists or ARBs: monitor potassium regularly.

src.q: Patients at risk for the development of hyperkalaemia include those with renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, hypoaldosteronism
Potassium sparing diuretics and angiotensin receptor blockers should be used with caution in patients receiving ACE inhibitors, and serum potassium and renal function should be monitored

items.t: Insulin autoimmune syndrome (including severe hypoglycaemia) has been reported; stop captopril if suspected.

src.q: Cases of Insulin Autoimmune Syndrome (IAS), including severe hypoglycaemic events have been reported during the treatment with captopril
If IAS is suspected, captopril should be discontinued

items.t: Aortic or mitral stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: use with caution. Avoid in cardiogenic shock and haemodynamically significant obstruction.

src.q: ACE inhibitors should be used with caution in patients with left ventricular valvular and outflow tract obstruction.
the use of captopril should be avoided in cases of cardiogenic shock and haemodynamically significant obstruction.

items.t: Dual RAAS blockade (with an ARB or aliskiren) not recommended; ACE inhibitors and ARBs should not be combined in diabetic nephropathy.

src.q: Dual blockade of RAAS through the combined use of ACE-inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers or aliskiren is therefore not recommended
ACE-inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers should not be used concomitantly in patients with diabetic nephropathy.

items.t: Diabetes on oral antidiabetics or insulin: monitor blood glucose closely, especially in the first month.

src.q: namely during the first month of treatment with an ACE inhibitor.

items.t: Hepatic failure (rare): stop if jaundice or marked liver enzyme rise.

src.q: Patients receiving ACE inhibitors who develop jaundice or marked elevations of hepatic enzymes should discontinue the ACE inhibitor and receive appropriate medical follow-up.

items.t: Proteinuria, mainly with existing renal disease or doses above 150 mg/day; check urine protein (dipstick, first morning urine) before and periodically in patients with prior renal disease.

src.q: Patients with evidence of prior renal disease should have urinary protein estimations (dip-stick on first morning urine) prior to treatment, and periodically thereafter.

items.t: Anaphylactoid reactions with high-flux dialysis membranes or LDL apheresis with dextran sulfate (avoid this combination), and during venom desensitisation (caution).

src.q: Therefore, this combination should be avoided.
caution should be used in patients treated with ACE inhibitors undergoing such desensitisation procedures.

items.t: Combined with a thiazide, hypokalaemia can still occur: monitor potassium regularly. Lithium: not recommended. Persistent dry cough can occur. Less effective in black patients. Hypotension during major surgery or anaesthesia can be corrected by volume expansion.

src.q: The combination of an ACE inhibitor with a thiazide diuretic does not rule out the occurrence of hypokalaemia.
Captopril is not recommended in association with lithium due to the potentiation of lithium toxicity
If hypotension occurs, it may be corrected by volume expansion.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, amiloride), potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, trimethoprim and co-trimoxazole: significant rise in potassium. Combination not recommended; if needed, use with caution and monitor potassium frequently.

src.q: potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes may lead to significant increase in serum potassium.

Therefore, the combination of captopril with the above-mentioned drugs is not recommended. If concomitant use is indicated, they should be used with caution and with frequent monitoring of serum potassium.

items.t: Dual RAAS blockade with angiotensin II receptor blockers (or aliskiren): more hypotension, hyperkalaemia and reduced renal function, including acute renal failure. Not recommended.

src.q: is associated with a higher frequency of adverse events such as hypotension, hyperkalaemia and decreased renal function (including acute renal failure)

items.t: NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen): additive rise in potassium and possible fall in renal function; rarely acute renal failure, especially in the elderly or dehydrated. Long-term NSAIDs may reduce the antihypertensive effect.

src.q: Rarely, acute renal failure may occur, particularly in patients with compromised renal function such as the elderly or dehydrated.
Chronic administration of NSAIDs may reduce the antihypertensive effect of an ACE inhibitor.

items.t: Insulin and oral antidiabetics (e.g. sulfonylureas): increased glucose lowering; the antidiabetic dose may need reducing. Monitor glucose closely in the first month.

src.q: can potentiate the blood glucose-reducing effects of insulin and oral antidiabetics such as sulfonylurea in diabetics.
it may be necessary to reduce the dose of the antidiabetics during simultaneous treatment with ACE inhibitors.

items.t: Thiazide or loop diuretics: prior high-dose diuretics can cause volume depletion and hypotension when captopril is started; reduce by stopping the diuretic, increasing volume or salt intake, or starting at a low captopril dose.

src.q: The hypotensive effects can be reduced by discontinuation of the diuretic, by increasing volume or salt intake or by initiating therapy with a low dose of captopril.

items.t: Alpha-blockers: greater antihypertensive effect and orthostatic hypotension. Other antihypertensives: increased hypotensive effect. Nitrates and other vasodilators: use with caution. Tricyclic antidepressants: enhanced hypotensive effect, postural hypotension. Sympathomimetics: may reduce the antihypertensive effect; monitor carefully.

src.q: Treatment with nitroglycerine and other nitrates, or other vasodilators (such as minoxidil), should be used with caution.
May reduce the anti-hypertensive effects of ACE inhibitors: patients should be carefully monitored.

items.t: Allopurinol, procainamide, cytostatic or immunosuppressive agents: increased risk of leucopenia.

src.q: Concomitant administration with ACE inhibitors may lead to an increased risk for leucopenia especially when the latter are used at higher than currently recommended doses.

items.t: Racecadotril, mTOR inhibitors and vildagliptin: higher angioedema risk; take care when starting them in a patient on an ACE inhibitor. Sacubitril/valsartan: contraindicated.

src.q: Caution should be used when starting racecadotril, mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, everolimus, temsirolimus) and vildagliptin in a patient already taking an ACE inhibitor.

items.t: Lithium: not recommended; if necessary, monitor lithium levels carefully. Ciclosporin or heparin: monitor potassium. Probenecid reduces captopril renal clearance. Clonidine switch may delay effect. May be used with aspirin (cardiac doses), thrombolytics, beta-blockers and nitrates after MI.

src.q: Use of captopril with lithium is not recommended, but if the combination proves necessary, careful monitoring of serum lithium levels should be performed
The renal clearance of captopril is reduced in the presence of probenecid.

items.t: Daily dose by creatinine clearance (SmPC table, units given as mL/min/1.73 m²; section 4.4 gives the 40 threshold in mL/min): above 40, start 25-50 mg, maximum 150 mg; 21-40, start 25 mg, maximum 100 mg; 10-20, start 12.5 mg, maximum 75 mg; below 10, start 6.25 mg, maximum 37.5 mg. Reduce dose or extend interval in renal impairment.

src.q: When concomitant diuretic therapy is required, a loop diuretic (e.g. Furosemide), rather than a thiazide diuretic, is preferred in patients with severe renal impairment.

items.t: The SmPC also says patients with renal impairment should not normally be treated with captopril; assess renal function (potassium, creatinine) before and during treatment.

Evaluation of the patient should include assessment of renal function (monitoring of potassium and creatinine) prior to initiation of therapy and at appropriate intervals thereafter.

items.t: SPS: seek specialist advice before starting if eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m².

items.t: Removed by haemodialysis in adults; not adequately cleared by peritoneal dialysis.

src.q: Captopril is not adequately cleared by peritoneal dialysis.

items.t: No hepatic dose adjustment stated. Rarely, ACE inhibitors cause cholestatic jaundice progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis; stop if jaundice or marked liver enzyme rise.

Patients receiving ACE inhibitors who develop jaundice or marked elevations of hepatic enzymes should discontinue the ACE inhibitor

items.t: SmPC: do not start in pregnancy; not recommended in the first trimester; contraindicated in the second and third trimesters. Stop as soon as pregnancy is diagnosed and switch if appropriate. If exposed from the second trimester, ultrasound check of fetal renal function and skull; observe the newborn for hypotension.

src.q: ACE inhibitors should not be initiated during pregnancy.
The use of ACE inhibitors is not recommended during the first trimester of pregnancy
The use of ACE inhibitors is contraindicated during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
Should exposure to ACE inhibitors have occurred from the second trimester of pregnancy, ultrasound check of renal function and skull is recommended.

items.t: MHRA: ACE inhibitors should not be used at any stage of pregnancy unless absolutely necessary; on diagnosis of pregnancy, stop as soon as possible.

src.q: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor antagonists should not be used at any stage of pregnancy unless absolutely necessary
On diagnosis of pregnancy, treatment with an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist should be stopped as soon as possible

items.t: BUMPS (ACE inhibitors, captopril named): early-pregnancy use is unlikely to harm the baby; use after about 20 weeks can cause problems in the baby and needs extra monitoring of amniotic fluid and fetal growth if continued.

src.q: Taking an ACE-I in early pregnancy is unlikely to harm your baby.
Taking an ACE-I after around 20 weeks of pregnancy can cause a number of problems in your baby
If you continue to take an ACE-I after around 20 weeks you will require additional monitoring to assess amniotic fluid levels and your baby's growth and wellbeing.

items.t: SmPC section 4.3 lists lactation as a contraindication. items.t: MHRA (2009): captopril not recommended in the first few weeks after delivery (risk of profound neonatal hypotension; preterm babies at particular risk); may be considered when the infant is older if an ACE inhibitor is needed, with careful infant follow-up for hypotension. MHRA clarification (2009): ACE inhibitors are not absolutely contraindicated in breastfeeding and may be prescribed if essential for the mother.

src.q: captopril, enalapril, or quinapril: use in breastfeeding is not recommended in the first few weeks after delivery because of the possibility of profound neonatal hypotension
use may be considered when the infant is older if an ACE inhibitor is necessary for the mother; careful follow-up of the infant for possible signs of hypotension is recommended
they are not absolutely contraindicated. Healthcare professionals may prescribe these medicines during breastfeeding if they consider that this treatment is essential for the lactating mother.

items.t: SPS (2023, no captopril-specific entry): enalapril is the preferred ACE inhibitor in breastfeeding; most ACE inhibitors can be used if clinically appropriate.

src.q: Enalapril is the preferred angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor during breastfeeding
most ACE inhibitors can be used during breastfeeding if clinically appropriate.

items.t: Planning pregnancy: switch to an antihypertensive with an established pregnancy safety profile unless continued ACE inhibitor treatment is essential.

src.q: Unless continued ACE inhibitor therapy is considered essential, patients planning pregnancy should be changed to alternative antihypertensive treatments which have an established safety profile for use in pregnancy.

items.t: Common: insomnia; taste disturbance and dizziness; dry cough and dyspnoea; nausea, vomiting, epigastric discomfort, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation, dry mouth; pruritus with or without rash, alopecia.
